s1.syndrome_frame: Asymptomatic swelling of the palate in an infant with a firm, nonmobile mass
salient_findings: Firm, nonmobile mass in the right posterior hard palate
Expansile lesion of the maxillary crest with mixed radiolucent and radiopaque internal structure
Thinning and perforation of the maxillary sinus walls and lateral displacement of the nasal cavity wall
key_facts: 10-month-old male infant
Asymptomatic swelling of the palate
Swelling was first noticed several weeks earlier
No swelling was noted at birth
Firm, nonmobile mass in the right posterior hard palate
Mass extends from the maxillary tuberosity medially almost to the midline
Multi-detector CT of the maxilla demonstrated a well-defined, expansile lesion
Lesion has mixed radiolucent and radiopaque internal structure
Maxillary sinus walls are thinned and perforated
Nasal cavity wall is laterally displaced

Ossifying fibromyxoid tumor of the jaw
Chronic sclerosing osteomyelitis of the jaw

shortlist.label: Cemento-ossifying fibroma
shortlist.why_kept: Radiographic findings of a well-defined, expansile lesion with mixed radiolucent and radiopaque internal structure match this diagnosis

shortlist.label: Fibrous dysplasia
shortlist.why_kept: Clinical presentation of a firm, nonmobile mass in the palate and radiographic findings of a lesion with mixed radiolucent and radiopaque internal structure are consistent with this diagnosis

shortlist.label: Odontogenic myxoma
shortlist.why_kept: Asymptomatic swelling of the palate and radiographic findings of a well-defined, expansile lesion are consistent with this diagnosis

shortlist.label: Central giant cell granuloma
shortlist.why_kept: Clinical presentation of a firm, nonmobile mass in the palate and radiographic findings of a lesion with mixed radiolucent and radiopaque internal structure are consistent with this diagnosis

shortlist.label: Cherubism
shortlist.why_kept: Asymptomatic swelling of the palate and radiographic findings of a well-defined, expansile lesion are consistent with this diagnosis, although less common in infants

raw.rationale: The lesion's well-defined, expansile nature with a mixed radiolucent and radiopaque internal structure, as seen on CT, is consistent with a cemento-ossifying fibroma, which is a benign fibro-osseous lesion that can cause expansion and thinning of the surrounding bone.

rejected.label: Fibrous dysplasia
rejected.why: Fibrous dysplasia typically presents with a ground-glass appearance on radiographs, which is not described in this case.

rejected.label: Odontogenic myxoma
rejected.why: Odontogenic myxomas are typically radiolucent and do not have the mixed radiolucent and radiopaque internal structure described in this case.

rejected.label: Central giant cell granuloma
rejected.why: Central giant cell granulomas are often associated with pain or tenderness, which is not reported in this asymptomatic case.

rejected.label: Cherubism
rejected.why: Cherubism typically presents with bilateral expansion of the mandible and maxilla, which is not described in this case with a unilateral lesion.
